events.title: Erlang/OTP 28 released
events.summary: The Erlang/OTP team released OTP 28 on May 21, 2025 with improved JIT, JSON enhancements, and Erlang shell improvements.
events.about: OTP 28 continued BEAM VM evolution for Elixir and Erlang production systems — faster JIT code paths, stdlib refinements, and better tooling for observability. It supports the growing Elixir adoption in fintech, messaging, and embedded Nerves devices.

narrative.whyChosen: OTP 28 keeps the BEAM competitive for high-availability distributed systems.
narrative.whyImportant: Incremental VM gains compound across every Phoenix and RabbitMQ deployment.
narrative.problemSolved: Long-running BEAM services need regular performance and security updates without breaking changes.

events.title: Anthropic Claude 4 Opus and Sonnet released
events.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 on May 22, 2025 — hybrid reasoning models with extended thinking, parallel tool use, and state-of-the-art coding scores.
events.about: Claude 4 made extended thinking with tool use a default capability and shipped Claude Code to general availability. Opus 4 led SWE-bench and long-running agent tasks; Sonnet 4 balanced cost and capability for everyday coding — intensifying the three-way race with OpenAI o3 and Gemini 2.5.

narrative.whyChosen: Claude 4 paired frontier coding with production-ready agent tooling.
narrative.whyImportant: Parallel tools and memory files pushed agentic coding from demo to daily workflow.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers needed models that could sustain multi-hour coding and research sessions reliably.
